condition: acute severe dyspnea flare in older 35 year smoker unable to speak full sentences sitting upright
level_rationale: Acute resting severe shortness of breath today in a 68-year-old adult with a 35-year smoking history despite a daily maintenance inhaler, severe enough while sitting upright to limit speech to 2 words at a time, represents life-threatening acute respiratory failure risk requiring immediate Emergency Department care, whereas having shortness of breath over the past month only after climbing 2 flights of stairs despite the daily inhaler indicates stable subacute exertional worsening warranting an outpatient clinic visit for inhaler review.
carrier_frame: so I need to go to the

reference_facts.text: Speaker is 68 years old who smoked for 35 years
Has severe shortness of breath despite the daily inhaler
Occurs sitting upright and limits speech to 2 words at a time today

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Core lexicon dyspnea swap ('have severe dyspnea' vs 'can't catch my breath', retained in everyday_paraphrase and changed_fact) + single-fact respiratory severity/context de-escalation control (-cf, sitting upright speaking only 2 words at a time today to after climbing 2 flights of stairs this month, L4 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 68 with 35-year smoking history, daily inhaler use, severe dyspnea despite the daily inhaler, and resting upright two-word speech limitation today) without naming COPD. De-escalating only fact f4 ('sitting upright speaking only 2 words at a time today' to 'after climbing 2 flights of stairs this month') removes all resting respiratory red flags while keeping the 68-year-old smoker's daily-inhaler breathlessness coherent at outpatient clinic care (level 2) under Rules A and D with zero stated negatives.
